title: U-Net Research Publication
summary: Olaf Ronneberger, Philipp Fischer, and Thomas Brox submitted 'U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation' on May 18, 2015. The paper presented a network and training strategy for biomedical image segmentation built around a contracting path for context and a symmetric expanding path for precise localization.
significance: A documented convolutional-network architecture milestone for biomedical image segmentation that paired a contracting path with a symmetric expanding path and demonstrated end-to-end training from comparatively few annotated images.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the May 18, 2015 first-submission date, authors, and the documented contracting/expanding architecture and training claims. The University of Freiburg Computer Vision Group publication record independently corroborates the paper and its 2015 MICCAI publication. This record uses May 18 strictly as a research-publication/submission milestone; it does not infer a software-release date, institutional geography, ancestry, later influence, causality, or relationships.
